sessions.title: MCP Auth Sessions
sessions.subtitle: Per-user credentials stored for MCP servers (OAuth tokens and submitted headers), plus any pending authentication flows.

col.typeTooltip: OAuth: per-user OAuth credential, either a stored token from a completed sign-in, or a pending sign-in flow. Headers: per-user header values (API keys / signed tokens), either stored or pending submission.
col.boundToTooltip: The identity this credential is keyed to: an end user (via SSO), a virtual key (shared by anyone using that VK), or a client-issued session ID (asserted via the x-bf-mcp-session-id header).
col.statusTooltip: Active: credential valid and usable. Pending: OAuth flow in progress, user must complete sign-in. Needs re-auth: upstream credential expired or revoked at the provider; user must reconnect. Needs update: the admin changed the required header keys; user must resubmit. Orphaned: the user lost access to this MCP (e.g. an access profile change); credential is preserved and will become Active automatically if access is restored.
col.scopesTooltip: Scopes the provider granted at sign-in, as reported in its token response. Shown as a dash when the provider did not report them. Header submissions and pending sign-ins have no scopes.
col.tokenExpiryTooltip: When the current access token expires. With a refresh token, Bifrost renews it on the next request, so an active row past its expiry silently mints a new token at use time. Without one, a past expiry means the row must be re-authenticated. Header rows do not have an upstream expiry; their values stay valid until revoked or the schema changes.
col.refreshTokenTooltip: Whether the provider issued a refresh token. Present: Bifrost renews the access token automatically at use time. Not issued: the row must be re-authenticated once the access token expires. Rejected upstream: the provider refused the last refresh, so the row needs re-auth. Header rows and pending sign-ins have no token.

empty.none: No sessions yet. Sessions appear here when an inference request or MCP gateway call triggers per-user authentication (OAuth or header submission).

sessions.revokeDesc: Bifrost will remove the stored credential for this binding. The upstream OAuth token is not revoked at the provider; it stays detached and expires naturally. Anyone using this binding will need to re-authenticate to obtain a fresh token.
sessions.revokeHeaderDesc: Bifrost will remove the stored credential values for this binding. There is no upstream token to revoke; the user will need to resubmit their header values to use this MCP again.

table.stateTooltip: The client's connection state (healthy, unstable, needs re-authorization, and so on). "Unstable" reflects Bifrost's own connection checks to the server, not the results of tool calls made through it: it self-heals and never blocks tool calls. For per-user clients (OAuth, headers, token exchange), this reflects Bifrost's own retained admin credential (used only to periodically refresh the tool list), not any individual user's own session, which is unaffected either way.
table.reregDesc: Bifrost will register a new OAuth client with this server's provider and run the consent flow against it, replacing the client it currently uses. Use this when the provider no longer recognises the client it issued, which shows up as "invalid_client" on refresh and leaves a plain reauthorize unable to recover the connection.
table.reregPerUserSuffix: Every user of this server will be signed out and will have to authenticate again.
table.reregSharedSuffix: Every credential currently issued for this server will be signed out.
table.reregTail: Otherwise use Reauthorize, which keeps the current client.
table.removeDesc: Are you sure you want to remove MCP server {{name}}? You will need to reconnect the server to continue using it.
table.oauthVerifiedToast: OAuth setup verified successfully. Each user will authenticate individually.
table.headersVerifiedToast: Headers verified successfully. Each user will submit their own values when using this MCP server.

state.pendingTokenExchange: This server needs a one-time verification: Bifrost exchanges your signed-in identity token, tests the connection, and discovers tools. Callers then have their own identity tokens exchanged automatically on every tool call.
state.pendingPerUserOauth: This client was declared in config.json. An admin sign-in is needed to verify the OAuth setup and discover tools; Bifrost keeps it on file to refresh the tool list periodically. Each user will still authenticate individually when they use this server.
state.pendingDefault: This client was declared in config.json and needs a one-time OAuth authorization before it can be used.
state.reauthTokenExchange: The admin credential Bifrost keeps on file to refresh this server's tool list needs repair. Callers' tool calls are unaffected. Use Re-verify as me from the server's actions menu to fix it.
state.reauthPerUser: The admin credential Bifrost keeps on file to refresh this server's tool list needs repair. End-user credentials and tool calls are unaffected. Use Refresh admin credential from the server's actions menu to fix it.
state.reauthDefault: This connection's credentials need to be re-authorized. Use Reauthorize from the server's actions menu to redo the OAuth consent flow.
state.unstableFailure: Bifrost's last connection check failed {{duration}} ago while {{stage}}. Tool calls are still attempted normally; the next check runs within about 10 seconds.
state.unstableNoFailure: Bifrost's last connection check failed. Tool calls are still attempted normally; the next check runs within about 10 seconds.
state.degraded: Instances of this deployment disagree about this server's state. Tool calls are still attempted on every instance.

usageGuide.emptySelectVk: Select a virtual key to continue.

auth.vkDesc: The client sends a virtual key header. Governance, budgets and tool access follow the key you pick below.
auth.oauthDesc: No credential in the config. The client discovers the gateway, opens Bifrost's consent page in a browser, and holds a short-lived token of its own.
auth.idpDesc: The client sends its caller's own SSO access token. Replace the placeholder with a token from your identity provider; the request is attributed to that user.

library.title: MCP Server Library
library.subtitle: Browse and install MCP servers from the synced catalog.

settings.title: MCP Library Settings
settings.desc: Configure the sync source and interval for the MCP server catalog.
settings.urlHint: URL to a custom MCP server catalog. Leave empty to use the default Bifrost catalog. For air-gapped deployments, set a file:// URL in config.json.
settings.intervalHint: How often to sync the MCP server catalog from the source URL. Set to 0 to disable background syncing; Force Sync Now still works.
settings.loadFailed: Unable to load current settings. Please retry.
settings.urlSchemeError: URL must start with http:// or https:// (file:// URLs can only be set in config.json)
settings.intervalMax: Sync interval cannot exceed 8760 hours (1 year)
settings.intervalMin: Sync interval must be 0 (disabled) or at least 1 hour

library.emptyNoSyncBody: Configure the library sync source in Settings to populate this catalog.
library.emptyNoMatchBody: Try adjusting your search or filters.
library.deleteCustomDesc: This custom server will no longer be available for members to install.
library.deleteSyncedDesc: This server will be hidden from the library and will not reappear on the next catalog sync.
library.headersConnected: {{name}} MCP server connected with per-user headers.
library.incompleteEntryDesc: This entry has no connection target. Ask the publisher to update the listing.
library.installDesc: Connect this library server to Bifrost and supply the credentials it needs.
library.nameRoutingHint: Bifrost uses this name internally when routing MCP tool calls.
library.oauthStartsNext: OAuth authorization starts after this step.
library.headersStartsNext: Header verification starts after this step.
library.toolsEnabledNote: All discovered tools will be enabled after install.
library.addDesc: Add a reusable server listing that members can discover and install. Nothing connects to Bifrost until someone installs it.
library.addNotice: This listing stays in your organization's library. It is not published to the global Bifrost MCP catalog. It is also a catalog entry, not a live MCP connection: credentials are never stored on the listing, each person who installs it supplies their own.

installHelp.headers: Add the request headers Bifrost should send with each tool call.
installHelp.oauth: Create the MCP client, then complete the OAuth authorization flow.
installHelp.perUserOauth: Create the MCP client, then authorize the first user OAuth connection.
installHelp.perUserHeaders: Declare the header names each caller must supply, then verify a sample set on install.
installHelp.tokenExchange: Set the identity-provider audience for this server; each caller's identity token is exchanged automatically.
installHelp.none: No credentials are required for this catalog entry.

add.listingDesc: How this server appears to members browsing the library.
add.connectionDesc: How Bifrost will reach this server once a member installs the listing.
add.namesOnlyHint: Names only; whoever installs the listing supplies the values.
add.authDesc: The scheme this server expects. It prefills the install form; no secrets are stored on the listing.
add.discoveryDesc: Optional metadata used to browse, filter, and attribute this listing.
